$comment: Machine-readable lab facts. Prose, provenance and the traps live in LAB.md next to this file. STRICT JSON on purpose - no comments - so any script or tool can read it without a lenient parser. Every value here was read from the machine or its RetroCore.ini, never assumed; LAB.md records how each was established and what is still unverified.

machines.note: Added 2026-08-09 because Ronny said so. NOT a RetroCore SINTRAN machine - a high-level Ethernet controller emulator another agent is writing, so folder/exe/disk/terminalPort may never apply. He has already defined it by hand on D100 and D102. UNVERIFIED BY US: whether it sits on hub 127.0.0.1:5010 like the others, and whether it answers anything. Nothing here was read off a machine, which is why every field we do not know is null rather than guessed.

tools.captureFilter: tcp port 10362 or tcp port 10364 or tcp port 10366

sintran.login: SYSTEM with an empty password; send name, CR, CR in ONE write
bringUpSequence: DEFINE-REMOTE-NAME,,<name>,<number>   for EVERY system including our own
START-LINK,1360,,,-1,,                LU is OCTAL, -1 means retry forever
sintran.adjacencyRule: COSMOS Operator Guide ND-30.025.02 section 2.5.4: a system on the far end of your own cable is ADJACENT and must NOT be given a route. Giving one is what made every peer unreachable.
sintran.restart: SINTRAN-SERVICE then STOP-XMSG then START-XMSG. This CLEARS the whole name table, including the machine's own name, so the bring-up sequence must be re-run in full.
